trial_court: VI Assistant Judge, City Civil Court, and C.R.P. No. 751 of 1972
case_name: Dr. H.T. Veera Reddi vs Smt. Kistamma
facts_of_case: Marriage took place in 1943. Wife filed O.P. No. 25 of 1970 for maintenance. Husband filed O.P. No. 48 of 1971 for restitution of conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: The Court has power to grant an injunction restraining a party from proceeding with a suit in a different court under the jurisdiction of a different High Court.
legal_principles.held: Thus it is clear that the principle evolved by the Supreme Court is that the Court has power both under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 and Section 151, Civil Procedure Code to grant an injunction restraining the party concerned from proceeding with the suit in a different Court under the jurisdiction of a different High Court.
cited_cases: Ram Bahadur Thakur and Company v. Devidayal (Sales) Limited

legal_principles.principle: The Court has power to grant an injunction independently of the Code of Civil Procedure.
legal_principles.held: Rash Behary Dey v. Bhowani Churn Base (1907) I.L.R. 34 Cal. 97, the Calcutta High Court has held in a suit filed in the High Court for specific performance of an agreement for lease of certain premises that the High Court has power under its general equity jurisdiction to grant an injunction of the character, independently of the Code of Civil Procedure.
cited_cases: Rash Behary Dey v. Bhowani Churn Base (1907) I.L.R. 34 Cal. 97

outcome.final_order: The petition was pending before the VI Assistant Judge, City Civil Court.

use_for_drafting: advising on restitution of conjugal rights
